top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on one specific idea, Katori's magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the differential light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, and on its realization at the 10^-18 level, which has been reproduced independently in Sr, Yb and Hg at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE. The two-name credit (Katori, Ye) is the cleanest on the shortlist, the citation can be worded on what has been demonstrated without relying on the pending redefinition of the second, and the clocks already deliver measured consequences such as millimetre-scale redshift resolution and many-body studies inside a clock. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the unrecognised early milestones of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Hinkley are real reservations, but they do not outweigh a mature, reproduced achievement, so an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile's superconducting-circuit and WACQT ties are not connected to optical lattice clocks, though my first opening choice (circuit QED) is no longer in play.
